chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Aban, from Ismail al-Ju'fi, from Umar ibn Hanzala, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What is the ruling on the Qunut on the day of Friday?' He said: 'You are my messenger to them regarding this: when you pray Salat in a congregation, it is in the first Rak'at, and when you pray Salat alone, it is in the second Rak'at before the Rukū'.'
ai.seo_question: When should the Qunut be recited during Friday prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the jurisprudential distinction between congregational and individual Friday prayers regarding the placement of the Qunut supplication, a ruling derived from the Imam’s instruction to Umar ibn Hanzala as his envoy. It highlights the practical application of ritual purity and timing in Shia fiqh, emphasizing that the supplication occurs before the bowing (ruku) in both scenarios, thereby ensuring the supplication is offered while standing in a state of readiness before the prostration sequence. This narration is foundational for understanding the procedural nuances of the Friday prayer (Salat al-Jumu'ah) in Twelver Shia tradition.
